questions.question: Statements: All pens are books. Some books are files. No file is a chair. Conclusions: I. Some pens are files. II. No pen is a chair.
questions.solution: Some books being files does not force any pen to be a file. Also, pens need not be files, so no relation between pens and chairs is definite. Neither follows.

questions.question: Statements: Some cars are buses. All buses are vehicles. No vehicle is a bicycle. Conclusions: I. Some cars are vehicles. II. No bus is a bicycle.
questions.solution: Some cars are buses and all buses are vehicles, so some cars are vehicles. Since no vehicle is a bicycle and all buses are vehicles, no bus is a bicycle.

questions.question: If A > B ≥ C = D < E, which conclusion is definitely true?

questions.question: Given P ≤ Q < R = S > T, which of the following is definitely false?
questions.solution: P≤Q<R=S, hence P<S. Therefore P>S is definitely false.

questions.question: In a code, MARKET is written as NBSLFU. How will PLANET be written in the same code?
questions.solution: Each letter is replaced by the next alphabet letter: P→Q, L→M, A→B, N→O, E→F, T→U.

questions.question: Pointing to a woman, Ravi said, 'She is the daughter of the only son of my grandfather.' How is the woman related to Ravi, if Ravi is male?

questions.question: What is the central idea of the passage?
options: Digital payments should completely replace cash immediately.
Digital payments offer important benefits to small businesses, but effective adoption also requires security awareness and infrastructure.
Online fraud makes digital payments unsuitable for small businesses.
Formal credit is available only to merchants who accept digital payments.
Customers benefit from digital payments while merchants do not.
questions.solution: The passage balances benefits with the need for awareness, trust and infrastructure.
questions.sharedStem:
Read the passage carefully and answer the questions.
Digital payments have changed the way small businesses handle everyday transactions. A shopkeeper who once depended entirely on cash can now receive money instantly through a phone, maintain a clearer record of sales, and reduce the need to keep large amounts of cash on the premises. For customers, digital payment is often faster and more convenient. Yet the transition is not without difficulty. Unstable internet connections, fear of online fraud, and limited digital literacy can discourage some users, particularly in areas where reliable technical support is scarce.

The benefits are greatest when technology is accompanied by awareness. Merchants who understand basic security practices—such as verifying payment notifications, using strong passwords, and refusing to share authentication codes—are less vulnerable to common scams. Training also helps users distinguish between a genuine failed transaction and a fraudulent request for another payment. Thus, expanding digital payments is not merely a matter of installing applications; it also requires trust, education and dependable infrastructure.

Despite these challenges, many small businesses continue to adopt digital methods because the advantages can be substantial. Transaction histories may help them understand sales patterns, plan purchases and, in some cases, demonstrate a financial record when seeking formal credit. The long-term value of digital payments therefore lies not only in speed but also in the information and opportunities that responsible use can create.

For customers, digital payment is often faster and more convenient. Yet the transition is not without difficulty. Unstable internet connections, fear of online fraud, and limited digital literacy can discourage some users, particularly in areas where reliable technical support is scarce.

The benefits are greatest when technology is accompanied by awareness. Merchants who understand basic security practices—such as verifying payment notifications, using strong passwords, and refusing to share authentication codes—are less vulnerable to common scams. Training also helps users distinguish between a genuine failed transaction and a fraudulent request for another payment. Thus, expanding digital payments is not merely a matter of installing applications; it also requires trust, education and dependable infrastructure.

Despite these challenges, many small businesses continue to adopt digital methods because the advantages can be substantial. Transaction histories may help them understand sales patterns, plan purchases and, in some cases, demonstrate a financial record when seeking formal credit. The long-term value of digital payments therefore lies not only in speed but also in the information and opportunities that responsible use can create.

questions.question: Identify the part containing an error: (A) Each of the applicants / (B) were asked to submit / (C) a valid identity proof / (D) before Friday. / (E) No error
questions.solution: 'Each' is singular; 'were' should be 'was'.

questions.question: Identify the part containing an error: (A) The committee has decided / (B) to postpone the meeting / (C) because several members / (D) are unavailable today. / (E) No error
questions.solution: The sentence is grammatically correct.

questions.question: Identify the part containing an error: (A) Neither the manager nor the employees / (B) was willing / (C) to accept the revised schedule / (D) without discussion. / (E) No error
questions.solution: With neither...nor, the verb agrees with the nearer subject 'employees'; use 'were willing'.

questions.question: Identify the part containing an error: (A) She has been working / (B) in this branch / (C) since / (D) three years. / (E) No error
questions.solution: Use 'for three years', not 'since three years'.

questions.question: Identify the part containing an error: (A) The new policy aims / (B) to reduce delays / (C) and improving / (D) customer satisfaction. / (E) No error
questions.solution: Parallel structure requires 'to reduce ... and improve', not 'and improving'.

questions.question: Choose the word that best completes the sentence: The bank introduced additional checks to _____ the risk of fraudulent transactions.

questions.question: Choose the word that best completes the sentence: Her explanation was so _____ that even a beginner could understand the process.
